subject: POC kickoff: multi-wave hands-on deep dives & load ops
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@skyforge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff availability across US/EU/APAC

Hi Ben / Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intros last week. SkyForge is eager to get the POC kicked off — we'd like hands-on technical deep dives that cover: prompt review, routing behavior for multi-tenant inputs, and a baseline load run to validate throughput and latency targets.

We need sessions that cover our three core teams across timezones. Proposed high-level windows (attached): proposed_windows.csv
- Wave 1 (Americas-friendly): Apr 20, 14:00–16:00 PDT
- Wave 2 (EMEA overlap): Apr 21, 09:00–11:00 CEST
- Wave 3 (APAC overlap): Apr 22, 10:00–12:00 SGT

Questions for you:
- Can Redwood run a baseline load test during one of the waves (we prefer Wave 1 or 3)?
- Can you dedicate ~30–45m in each session specifically for prompt engineering / prompt QA with our ML lead?
- Any constraints on routing demo tenants to dedicated instances (we care about isolating routing rules during load runs)?

Attached is the CSV with our preferred windows. If you can propose concrete slots in each wave, we can lock calendar invites.

Best,
Amy Chen
Head of Integrations, SkyForge AI
amy.chen@skyforge.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@skyforge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff availability across US/EU/APAC

Hey Amy — great to hear and thanks for the clear windows + CSV. We're aligned on the agenda items (prompt review, routing deep dive, baseline load).

High-level proposal from our side (I put the ask into a one-page MAP — attached: mutual-action-plan-v1.docx):
- Structure: 2-hour hands-on sessions per wave. First 60–75m focused on prompt review & routing logic (including sample traffic and routing rules), final 45–60m reserved for load validation and runbook walkthroughs.
- Rotation approach: we will rotate start times by ~8 hours across the three waves so you get the same agenda for each geo; that keeps the demos repeatable and lets us warm caches in between runs.
- Baseline load: Redwood can run the baseline using our dedicated test harness. We recommend baseline profiles of 50/200/500 concurrent simulated sessions. For the production-like test we suggest KV-cache warm-up of 10–15 minutes before the main ramp.

Can you confirm: preferred wave for the full production-like baseline? If you want it on Wave 1 (Americas) we can target Apr 20 14:30 PDT start for the load run.

Next steps:
1) We (Redwood) will publish specific slots for each wave by EOD.
2) Please confirm who from SkyForge will join the prompt review (name + title) so we can prepare targeted examples.
3) I'll create calendar invites once the slots are locked.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions – Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v1.docx

> Can you confirm: preferred wave for the full production-like baseline? If you want it on Wave 1 (Americas) we can target Apr 20 14:30 PDT start for the load run.

Amy / Team — quick concrete slots from infra and my schedule:
- Wave A (Americas-friendly): Apr 20 — 14:00–16:00 PDT (we reserve 14:30–15:15 for the baseline ramp & steady-state run).
- Wave B (EMEA): Apr 21 — 09:00–11:00 CEST (prompt review 09:00–10:00, routing deep dive 10:00–10:45, light sanity load test 10:45–11:00).
- Wave C (APAC): Apr 22 — 10:00–12:00 SGT (we can flip the order if APAC team prefers load first).

Operational notes:
- Baseline profiles we can execute: 50 concurrent (quick sanity), 200 concurrent (target), 500 concurrent (stress). Each profile includes a 10min warm-up and 20–30min steady-state measurement.
- We'll need a named list of prompt examples and routing rules by Apr 18 EOD to pre-seed caches and create deterministic test inputs.
- For routing isolation during tests, we can map SkyForge tenants to a dedicated routing lane in Redwood Dedicated during the POC windows. That requires a short network handoff; I will coordinate with Platform to reserve the lane.

I can create the calendar invites once Ben confirms the final preferred load window.

—Jordan
